subject: Post-call: Reducing false positives in ranker integration and evaluation next steps
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Sam Wong <sam.wong@acmeretail.com>; Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + technical clarifications (ranker integration)

Hi Sam / Priya —

Thanks again for the demo earlier — really helpful to see your current search flow and the examples of false positives you flagged. Per our call, I wanted to capture the asks and a short list of technical questions so Karthik and Neha can scope the integration work and an evaluation plan.

Quick recap / goals:
- Primary goal: reduce product list false positives in search and recommendations by tuning a reranker layer (relevance-first, preserve recall of promotional items).
- Success metrics: +15% relevance precision@10 for business-critical queries, <5% degradation in recall for curated promos, and mean reciprocal rank (MRR) lift where feasible.
- Timeline: pilot test in sandbox in 3 weeks, production rollout (canary) in 8–10 weeks once we validate quality and latency.

Immediate asks (please confirm):
1) Dataset: you said you can share a CSV of ~4k labeled queries and the current top-50 candidate set for each query. Confirm we should use the "acme-eval-prompts.csv" snapshot (attachment).
2) Auth / SDK: do you want us to use the Redwood Java SDK or call REST directly? You mentioned constrained outbound networking from your search cluster — is mutual TLS required?
3) Routing: will you run the reranker in-line in the search cluster (sync, <100ms extra budget), or route async to a separate service (we recommended sync for relevance-sensitive flows)?
4) Top_k tuning: is the candidate pool fixed at 50 per query, or do we need to support variable k per query type? Any queries where you only want top-5 considered?
5) Evaluation criteria: aside from precision@10 and MRR, are there internal KPIs (CTR lift, add-to-cart) you want included in the pilot?

Technical clarifications for Karthik (cc'd):
- Required model behavior: structured output for reranker scores (JSON with item_id + score + optional rationale string). We discussed using tool-calling style structured responses; confirm you can accept a small JSON blob back from the rerank call.
- Latency SLO: production SLO target is 100ms median for the rerank step; pilot can be up to 200ms.

Next steps:
- Sam / Priya: share the labeled dataset and a sanitized sample of candidate doc fields (sku, title, category, price).
- Redwood: Karthik to prototype ranking adapter and share an API spec (we attached redwood-ranker-api-spec.pdf).
- Schedule: propose a 60-min technical sync mid-next-week to walk the adapter code path and auth flow.

Attachments: redwood-ranker-api-spec.pdf, acme-eval-prompts.csv, mutual-action-plan.xlsx

Thanks — I captured these in HubSpot (link below). If anything's off, flag it here and I’ll update the doc.

— Rachel
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com

From: Sam Wong <sam.wong@acmeretail.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmeretail.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + technical clarifications (ranker integration)

Thanks Rachel — this is great and matches our notes. A few clarifications inline.

- Dataset: yes, attach is the sanitized eval CSV we discussed (acme-eval-prompts.csv). It contains 4,120 labeled queries with a gold set of SKUs. We will follow up with a separate sample export of candidate documents (top-50 per query) — that will be shared via Drive.
- Auth: our search cluster can do outbound HTTPS, but we require mTLS for any calls that carry PII/price-sensitive fields. For the pilot you can use token-based auth against a sandbox endpoint; production will need mTLS.
- Routing: prefer a sync inline rerank for the primary product search (latency sensitive). For secondary recommendation widgets we can look at async flows later.
- Top_k: candidate pool is usually 50 but some nav queries return only 10; we need the adapter to respect variable candidate k. Default top_k to min(50, candidate_count) for the pilot.
- Metrics: add CTR and add-to-cart (ATC) as secondary metrics for the evaluation.

We’ll upload the candidate sample and an internal metric spec to the Drive folder by Thursday. Mid-week technical sync works — Thurs 08/06 10am PT for our team.

— Sam
Sam Wong
Senior Search Eng, Acme Retail
sam.wong@acmeretail.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sam Wong <sam.wong@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + technical clarifications (ranker integration)

Hi Sam — thanks for the quick clarifications. A few follow-ups so we can size the engineering work: 

1) Auth requirements: for mTLS in prod, do you manage the certs on your side (preferred), or do you want Redwood to integrate with your internal PKI? If you manage certs, we'll provision a sandbox token flow for the pilot and add mTLS support in the adapter for production.

2) Candidate payload: please confirm the fields you can share in candidate docs. We prefer a compact payload: {item_id, title, description, category_id, price_cents, availability_flag, popularity_score}. If price is sensitive, we can accept hashed price bands.

3) Scoring schema & structured output: Redwood's ranking API returns scores as a JSON array (item_id + score as float 0..1). We can also emit a short "rationale" (one-line) for top-3 candidates to help triage. Is that acceptable for your trace/logging?

4) Evaluation: do you have an internal baseline MRR/precision snapshot we should target relative to? If not, we will compute baseline from the candidate export.

I’ll draft the adapter PR and post a short design doc to the Drive folder before the Thursday sync.

— Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood

From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmeretail.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 6 Aug 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + technical clarifications (ranker integration)

Karthik — quick answers from infra / search ops: 
- We will manage mTLS certs on our side and can provide an intermediate CA for Redwood to trust.
- Candidate payload: we can provide all the fields you listed but will remove SKU-level pricing in the initial sandbox; will provide price_band (LOW/MED/HIGH) instead.
- Baseline metrics: attached in Drive (baseline_metrics_202607.csv) — current precision@10 is 0.42 and MRR is 0.31 across the labeled set. Our internal team will expect a statistically significant lift over this baseline for the pilot to be successful.

Look forward to the design doc. See you on Thurs 10am PT.

— Priya
Product Lead, Search — Acme Retail

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Sam Wong <sam.wong@acmeretail.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 7 Aug 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + technical clarifications (ranker integration)

Thanks everyone — appreciate the quick turn. Action items I captured: 
1) Acme: upload Drive folder with candidate sample, baseline metrics, and the labeled CSV by Thu 08/06 (Sam/Priya).
2) Redwood: Karthik to post adapter design + sandbox API endpoint (redwood sandbox token) and sample code using Java SDK and curl.
3) Both: technical sync Thurs 08/06 10am PT — calendar invite sent (link in HubSpot).
4) Evaluation: Redwood will run an initial offline eval (precision@10, MRR) against your labeled set and return a short report (expected within 7 business days of candidate sample receipt).

I'll upload the mutual action plan and attach the DocuSign for the pilot SOW once we align on scope. Thanks — I'll follow up after the sync with the PR link and the sandbox token.

— Rachel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
